item.title: Fiji imports processed sugar for manufacturers- Tunabuna
item.description: Fiji imports processed white sugar for manufacturers such as Coca-Cola and other companies, while raw sugar for supermarkets is only imported when there is insufficient locally produced sugar. This was highlighted by Minister for Sugar Tomasi Tunabuna while speaking to fijivillage News, saying this is done particularly when production is low or after a natural disaster.
item.content:encoded:
Fiji imports processed white sugar for manufacturers such as Coca-Cola and other companies, while raw sugar for supermarkets is only imported when there is insufficient locally produced sugar.

This was highlighted by Minister for Sugar Tomasi Tunabuna while speaking to fijivillage News, saying this is done particularly when production is low or after a natural disaster.

Tunabuna says the Fiji Sugar Corporation (FSC) has reported that it has some stock available for supermarkets.

He says Fiji normally imports raw sugar when there is insufficient sugar, especially when production is low or when the country experiences a natural disaster.

Insert:Tunabuna on sugar import 29th July.

The Minister says white sugar, icing sugar and other processed sugars are all imported and are not made from Fiji's brown sugar.

He explains that Fiji produces raw sugar, while processed sugars are imported at all times.

Providing an update on the crushing season, the Minister says the Lautoka and Labasa mills are operating at above 80 percent of their capacity, while the Ba Mill is operating at a little over 60 percent capacity, adding that production is now picking up.

Meanwhile, the Minister also highlights efforts to support diversification among sugarcane farmers.

He says last week he handed over a project to a farming community involved in sugarcane, which can also be used for cultivating other crops.

He says more than 30 rice harvesters have been provided over the past three weeks.

The Minister says they are also looking at increasing the fertiliser subsidy to include other crops so they can continue providing assistance to sugarcane farmers, allowing them to benefit from growing other crops, not just sugarcane.

item.title: Opposition MP Vijay Nath calls for urgent Police action following attacks on taxi drivers in Wainibokasi
item.description: Following the recent increase in robberies and assaults against taxi drivers in Wainibokasi, Opposition MP, Vijay Nath has called the Government and the Police to take immediate and decisive action before the situation deteriorates further. Nath says Police must increase its visibility in crime-prone areas through regular foot patrols, mobile patrols and targeted policing operations, particularly
item.content:encoded:
Following the recent increase in robberies and assaults against taxi drivers in Wainibokasi, Opposition MP, Vijay Nath has called the Government and the Police to take immediate and decisive action before the situation deteriorates further.

Nath says Police must increase its visibility in crime-prone areas through regular foot patrols, mobile patrols and targeted policing operations, particularly around the Nausori Bus Stand, the mini-bus stand and surrounding areas where these incidents have been reported.

He says Police should also strengthen intelligence gathering, engage closely with taxi associations and business owners, and conduct regular operations to identify and apprehend repeat offenders.

Nath says a visible and proactive police presence will not only deter criminal activity but also restore public confidence that Nausori is a safe place to live, work and do business.

The Opposition MP says authorities must also take firm action against intoxicated people behaving aggressively or threatening taxi drivers and members of the public.

He says these attacks are no longer confined to the late hours of the night.

Nath says many drivers are refusing to operate after 7pm because they no longer feel safe.

He says t his is not just a problem for taxi operators and it affects workers trying to get home, students travelling to and from school, families, the elderly, businesses and the wider public who rely on taxis everyday.

Nath adds that when taxi drivers fear for their lives, the entire community suffers.

The Opposition MP says the time for action is now.

Responding to our questions, Assistant Commissioner of Police Operations Kasiano Vusonilawe says they are doing their best, in line with the resources and capabilities they have, through ongoing investigations and patrols.

Vusonilawe is urging taxi drivers to always take precautionary measures and, if they are suspicious of their passengers, to drive to the nearest Police Station or Community Post.

He adds that, regarding the installation of CCTV cameras, Police do not have the budget to facilitate CCTV coverage in every corner of a central business district, and they need the public's assistance in addressing the issues raised.

item.title: More than 400 laptops donated to boost digital learning in Fiji schools
item.description: Students at several schools across Fiji are set to benefit from improved access to digital learning after 450 laptops were distributed this week through a partnership between Dubai-based global logistics company DP World and Australian not-for-profit organisation LiteHaus International. The donation is expected to strengthen digital literacy, improve access to technology for classroom learning and
item.content:encoded:
Students at several schools across Fiji are set to benefit from improved access to digital learning after 450 laptops were distributed this week through a partnership between Dubai-based global logistics company DP World and Australian not-for-profit organisation LiteHaus International.

The donation is expected to strengthen digital literacy, improve access to technology for classroom learning and research, and better prepare students for tertiary education and an increasingly technology-driven workforce.

As part of the rollout, Suva Grammar School received 30 laptops.

Head Girl Anna Jikoibau says the additional laptops will ease pressure on existing resources.

Jikoibau says the donation will ensure more students can complete schoolwork independently while gaining valuable digital skills that will benefit them in the future.

Head Boy Brendan Leo says the donation will reduce the challenges caused by limited access to computers.

He also urged students to look after the devices and use them for their intended purpose.

Acting Vice Principal of Suva Grammar School, Ralifo Nasario welcomed the donation, saying it would help bridge the gap between students and technology and better prepare them for tertiary education and an increasingly digital future.

Nasario says the laptops will support Year 12 and 13 students who are required to complete research projects and typed assignments, while also allowing them to use artificial intelligence as a learning tool.

He says early exposure to technology is essential before students progress to tertiary education.

He also encouraged students to embrace technology responsibly, saying they need the understanding and capability to use AI effectively, adding that without knowledge of AI, they will be left behind.

Meanwhile, Stella Maris School and Davuilevu Methodist School also received 15 laptops each.

The remaining laptops were distributed to schools in the Western Division, including Maharishi Sanatan College, Maharishi Primary School, Votualevu College, Votualevu Public School, Sabeto Central Primary School, and Nadi Special Education Centre.

DP World Executive Vice President for Oceania, Nicolaj Noes says that as the company's presence in Fiji continues to grow, it remain committed to creating lasting value for local communities and supporting the country's long-term economic and social development.

Noes says students will also get access to DP World’s Global Education Platform (GEP), which hosts multiple e-learning modules on various topics.

Head of Program Delivery for LiteHaus International, Rob Birnie, says the organisation has now provided computers to 125 schools across Fiji, with this being its fourth rollout in the country.

He also thanked DP World for its ongoing support across the Pacific.

item.title: 13 confirmed dead after powerful Japan earthquake, rescue efforts continue
item.description: 13 people have been confirmed dead after a powerful earthquake struck south-west Japan, with rescue efforts continuing in the worst-hit areas. Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi confirms the death toll as emergency crews continued searching for survivors trapped under collapsed buildings.
item.content:encoded:
13 people have been confirmed dead after a powerful earthquake struck south-west Japan, with rescue efforts continuing in the worst-hit areas.

Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi confirms the death toll as emergency crews continued searching for survivors trapped under collapsed buildings.

Rescue teams are focusing on a shopping mall in Kumamoto, where a number of people remain trapped after the second floor reportedly collapsed during the quake.

Authorities have also confirmed that several people remain unaccounted for at the shopping centre and at a nearby factory where a chimney collapsed.

Emergency personnel, including firefighters and rescue workers, are continuing search and rescue operations as authorities warn residents to remain alert for possible aftershocks.

item.title: EMP application for beach manholes and trenching of conduits relating to proposed Natadola cable landing development declined
item.description: The Department of Environment declined the Environmental Management Plan application for the beach manholes and trenching of conduits relating to the proposed Natadola Google cable landing development in Malomalo, Nadroga on 5th February last year on the grounds of community concerns and objections, as well as insufficient social survey and public consultation information. Ba sed on public reactio
item.content:encoded:
The Department of Environment declined the Environmental Management Plan application for the beach manholes and trenching of conduits relating to the proposed Natadola Google cable landing development in Malomalo, Nadroga on 5th February last year on the grounds of community concerns and objections, as well as insufficient social survey and public consultation information.

Ba sed on public reactions, the Ministry of Environment clarifies the proposed development forms part of the Pacific Connect initiative, a regional telecommunications programme establishing new subsea cable links between Fiji and destinations including the United States, Australia and French Polynesia.

It says the project comprises three components: the proposed Landing Station Facility, to be constructed and developed by Staghorn Services Pte Limited, the installation of two beach manholes and associated conduits leading to the landing station facility, also by Staghorn Services Pte Limited, and the Marine Subsea Cable Landing, developed and managed by Yellowfin Infrastructure Pte Limited.

Three separate EIA screening applications were lodged with the Department, one for each component.

The Environment Ministry says each was assessed on its own merits, and the components should not be reported as a single approval or a single refusal.

For the beach manholes and trenching of conduits, the Department of Environment advised the proponent that these matters must be satisfactorily addressed before further consideration can be given to the application.

The regulatory status of the other two components is that the Environmental Management Plan has been approved with conditions on 19th July 2024 for the Landing Station Facility (Staghorn Services Pte Limited) and Environmental Management Plan has been approved with conditions on 23rd September 2024 for the Marine Subsea Cable Landing (Yellowfin Infrastructure Pte Limited).

The proposed cable route is located at Natadola Bay between the Yatule Resort and Spa and the InterContinental Fiji Golf Resort and Spa and extends approximately 1.3 kilometres inland along the access road to Maro Road to the proposed Landing Station Facility site.

As part of the assessment process, a Marine Ecological Resource Assessment was undertaken in 2024 to assess potential impacts on marine habitats, fish communities, birds and water quality.

The assessment found that the marine environment within the project area is characterized by fringing coral reefs, rubble, rock and sandy substrates, with ecological communities typical of Fiji's nearshore coastal environments.

To minimize environmental impacts, the conditions imposed for the marine cable component include restricting works to daylight hours, suspending earthworks during heavy rainfall and adverse weather, protecting seagrass meadows and marine habitats, requiring prompt reporting of spills, and ensuring that cable installation activities avoid adverse impacts on coastal and marine ecosystems.

The Department also required a social survey to assess community views on the proposed development.

That requirement was imposed by the determination letter issued to Staghorn Services Pte Limited on 29th April 2024 and related specifically to the beach manholes and trenching works.

The survey, undertaken on 28th June 2024, covered residents of Sanasana Village and stall operators at Natadola Beach.

Fifty households were visited and 28 were interviewed; the remaining 22 were unwilling to respond.

Four of the households interviewed opposed the proposal, citing adverse impacts on their surroundings, on tourist activity in the area, and on their income from selling to visitors.

The other respondents did not object, provided their businesses were not affected.

The Department subsequently identified concerns regarding the adequacy of the consultation process and requested additional engagement with affected stakeholders, including Vanua Naholo, the Ministry of Lands and Mineral Resources, the iTaukei Land Trust Board and the Nadroga Provincial Office.

This consultation was facilitated through the Nadroga Provincial Office on 6th February 2025.

On that day, the Ministry of Environment made it clear that it will not involve in any compensation discussions between FNPF (that represented Google) and the vanua, as this is beyond their regulatory mandate.

During the consultations, the vanua had indicated that they would be drafting a MOA for FNPF's consideration.

The vanua also requested that the Environmental Management Plan consultant and the proponent provide an information session on the project in its entirety so that they can ask any questions, and this was relayed to the consultant.

During the consultation, further information was requested on the marine coastal assessment and the lease arrangements.

The Department relayed this request to the EMP consultant and the project proponent.

The groundbreaking ceremony went ahead in 2024 for this proposed project although the approval process was under consideration.

Permanent Secretary, Doctor Sivendra Michael had earlier said that if the Environmental Impact Assessment is under consideration for proposed projects, the private sector should not run to the ministers to get things moving and do groundbreaking ceremonies ahead of all the required approvals.
